title: Aina Mahal - The Palace of Mirrors in Bhuj
content:
Aina Mahal, Bhuj

Nestled in the heart of Bhuj, Gujarat, Aina Mahal (meaning Palace of Mirrors) is one of the most magnificent examples of Indo-European architecture. Built during the 18th century, this grand palace reflects the royal taste and artistic excellence of Kutch’s rulers. Its intricate mirror work, ornate walls, and elegant designs make it a must-visit destination for history lovers and architecture enthusiasts.

History of Aina Mahal

The Aina Mahal was commissioned by Maharaja Lakhpatji in 1750, designed by the talented architect and craftsman Ram Singh Malam. Having spent several years in Europe, Ram Singh brought back European techniques and blended them beautifully with Indian craftsmanship, creating a fusion of Indian, Dutch, and Gothic styles.
Despite being damaged during the 2001 Bhuj earthquake, parts of the palace have been restored and preserved as a museum, showcasing the royal heritage of Kutch.

Architectural Highlights

  • Mirror Work: The interiors are adorned with thousands of Venetian mirrors that glitter in candlelight, giving the palace its name.
  • Belgian Glass & Tiles: Imported tiles, glass, and marble showcase European influence.
  • Ivory and Gold Inlay Work: The walls and doors feature intricate designs, with ivory and gold embellishments.
  • Durbar Hall: The grand hall displays royal possessions such as clocks, paintings, and musical instruments, taking visitors back to the glorious Kutch era.

Museum Collection

  • The Aina Mahal Museum houses an impressive collection of royal artifacts:
  • Vintage photographs and paintings of Kutch rulers.
  • Antique clocks and mechanical toys.
  • Handcrafted textiles and ornaments.
  • A 15-foot-long scroll painting depicting the royal processions.

Timings and Entry Fee

  • Timings: 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM
  • Closed on: Thursdays and public holidays
  • Entry Fee: ₹20 for Indians and ₹100 for foreign visitors

(Timings and fees may vary, so it’s best to check locally before visiting.)

Nearby Attractions

  • Prag Mahal: Located adjacent to Aina Mahal, this stunning Gothic-style palace is known for its high bell tower and grand arches. Read more..
  • Kutch Museum: The oldest museum in Gujarat, showcasing tribal culture and historical artifacts. Read more..
  • Hamirsar Lake: A peaceful spot for evening walks and local life views. Read more..
  • Bhujodi Village: Famous for its handwoven textiles and local handicrafts. Read more..

How to Reach Aina Mahal

  • Nearest Airport: Bhuj Airport (5 km away)
  • Nearest Railway Station: Bhuj Railway Station (3 km away)
  • By Road: Easily accessible by car, auto, or local transport from any part of Bhuj.

Best Time to Visit

The ideal time to visit Aina Mahal is between October and February, when the weather in Bhuj is pleasant for sightseeing.
